Nikhil / Vanessa — quick technical note I drafted to hand to Alicia's eng team. Copying the snippet into the thread so procurement sees the constraints too.

--- begin technical brief ---
Short answer on INT4 and summarization: INT4 often works well for encoder‑decoder and decoder‑only models *if* you do the following rollout:

1) Validation sweep: run 500 representative queries through FP16 baseline and INT4 candidate; measure ROUGE / semantic similarity (we prefer embedding cosine + human spot checks). Expect mean delta 0.5–1.5% for many summarization hashes; worst‑case spikes need guardrails.
2) Per‑route fallback: keep FP16 variant available for any request that fails a simple quality threshold; automatic routing costs a modest overhead (~2–5% tokens).
3) Prefix caching: enable KV caching only on non‑PII routes. Implement a tagging rule in your app that labels inputs for caching. We can route by tag in the platform.

Commercial implication: if you allow selective INT4 on 60% of traffic and KV caching on 70% of non‑PII routes, you should see ~45% unit cost reduction vs baseline.

Suggested pilot concession (internal): 3 months of $40k platform credit + 8 hours onboarding support from our Ops team. Alternatively, a 12% flat pilot discount if procurement prefers a discount.

--- end technical brief ---

Happy to present this live to their engineers — propose Thursday 11am PT.
